description:
## Question

What does the GitHub Actions free tier give a public repo, and where does it stop? The dual CI (GitHub Actions plus a local recipe, decided on the map 'Wayfinder: defk ready for a first Hex release') must fit inside these limits.

Find, from GitHub's own docs: minutes and cost for public repos on standard runners; Linux arm64 hosted runners (labels, availability for public repos, limits); macOS arm64 runners for public repos; concurrent job limits; job and workflow time limits; storage and cache limits; anything that throttles or stops a run (for example abuse limits).

Done when: the findings are in docs/research/ with sources, and the resolution comment states the limits that shape the CI matrix.

comments.text:
Resolution (GitHub docs and changelog, read 2026-10-14):
- Minutes are free and unlimited on standard GitHub-hosted runners in a public repo, including ubuntu-24.04 (x64, 4 vCPU/16 GB), ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64, 4 vCPU/16 GB, GA for public repos 2025-08-07) and macos-15/macos-26/macos-latest (arm64 M1, 3 cores/7 GB). Larger runners are always billed: use standard labels only.
- Concurrency is the binding limit: Free plan 20 concurrent jobs, at most 5 macOS. A 4-job run uses 4 slots and 1 macOS slot; use concurrency cancel-in-progress per branch.
- Time: 6 h per job (fails), 35 days per workflow run; ubuntu-slim has a 15 min cap, do not use it. Matrix max 256 jobs, 50 re-runs.
- Storage: cache 10 GB/repo, 7-day eviction of unused entries; artifacts 500 MB (shared with Packages), retention 1-90 days on public repos.
- Other stops: GITHUB_TOKEN 1,000 API req/h/repo, cache uploads 200/min, secondary rate limits, Actions acceptable-use terms (CI for the repo's own code is fine).
- The 4-job matrix on every push fits; macOS (5 slots, 7 GB RAM, slowest machine) is the tightest constraint.
Findings: branch research/gha-free-tier, docs/research/gha-free-tier.md

title: GitHub Actions free-tier limits for a public repo
